subject: Launch commit structure and surge caps for Nimbus Games
messages:
From: Laurie Park <laurie@nimbusgames.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbusgames.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:13:00 -0400
Subject: Pricing and monthly commit structure for launch ramp

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profiles and routing controls. We're starting to lock down pricing for our fall launch and need to finalize a monthly commit and surge policy. A few specific asks:

- We expect a 3-month ramp window (Aug–Oct) with substantial seasonality spikes in month 2. Can you propose a commit schedule that smooths costs but lets us handle 2x–3x bursts?
- We need a "cliff protection" or failure-safeguard option in case adoption is slower than forecast; would prefer a partial-month true-up rather than full penalty in months 1–2.
- Any chance to include limited rollover or credit for unused committed tokens into the next quarter?

Can you return a concrete monthly commit schedule and the per-token effective price at each step (including overage rates and surge caps)? Procurement also needs any SOW/attachments for review.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — legal wants a draft by end of next week.

Best,
Laurie Park
Head of Product Operations
Nimbus Games

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pricing and monthly commit structure for launch ramp

Hi Laurie — thanks, glad the demo landed well. I attached an initial SOW and a pricing workbook so you can see the mechanics. High level options below — I tried to cover conservative and aggressive ramps plus a hybrid with explicit surge caps.

Attachments: Nimbus_SOW_v1.pdf, pricing_calc_nimbus.xlsx

Option A — Aggressive 3-month step-up (lower blended unit cost if you hit ramp):
- Month 1 commit: 100M tokens
- Month 2 commit: 400M tokens (anticipated peak)
- Month 3 commit: 600M tokens
- Surge cap: 3x committed monthly volume allowed, billed at committed rate up to cap then overage at +40%

Option B — Phased 6-month smoothing (lower risk to you, slightly higher unit cost):
- Monthly commits ramp gradually from 100M -> 200M -> 300M over 6 months
- Surge cap: 2.5x

Option C — Base commit + burst buffer (hybrid):
- Base monthly commit: 150M
- Burst buffer pool: additional shared 600M across the first 3 months, used as credits
- True-up cadence: quarterly with rollover window of one quarter

Cliff protection: we can include a two-month mitigation window where unused commit in months 1–2 can be partially credited (50% credit) or converted to a discounted overage allowance for month 3.

I'll loop in Marissa (pricing lead) and Karthik (pricing ops/math) to propose final numbers and guardrails. If you can share the most conservative and most aggressive internal forecast numbers for Aug–Oct (even ballpark), we can lock a recommendation.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan

Laurie/Priya — looping in a couple of quick guardrail suggestions from a leader POV:

- Failure-safeguard / cliff protection: propose a two-part safety net: (1) first 60 days: flexible true-up with 50% credit on unused commit (as Priya suggested), (2) months 3–4: revert to standard quarterly true-up. This protects your launch while keeping economics sensible for both sides.
- Surge cap recommendation: set an absolute surge cap at 3x month-over-month for the launch period with an automated fallback to a cost-optimized smaller model variant if sustained beyond 48 hours.
- Rollover: allow unused commit to roll forward for one quarter only, capped at 25% of the next quarter's commit. This prevents accumulation abuse but gives you breathing room.

If this direction looks good, Karthik can produce a final per-token blended table and we can hand to Legal for contract language. Priya — please also flag if Finance wants prepayment language for the first month.

Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laurie Park <laurie@nimbusgames.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pricing and monthly commit structure for launch ramp — math and schedule

Laurie — quick calc and a recommended monthly schedule based on the three options. I attached the working spreadsheet (pricing_calc_nimbus.xlsx). Quoted per-token rates are net of volume discounts.

Assumptions: baseline per-token list price = $0.00008/token (hosted), volume breakpoints at 250M, 500M, 1B monthly tokens.

Recommended (hybrid, lowers risk but rewards ramp):
- Month 1 (Aug): commit = 125M tokens -> effective rate = $0.000075/token (5% discount)
- Month 2 (Sep): commit = 375M tokens -> effective rate = $0.0000625/token (22% discount)
- Month 3 (Oct): commit = 625M tokens -> effective rate = $0.000055/token (31% discount)
- Surge cap: 3x committed month volume. Overage beyond surge cap billed at list + 40% (i.e., $0.000112/token).

Quarterly true-up example: if actual tokens consumed in Q3 = 1.05B vs committed total = 1.125B, customer is credited per agreed true-up formula (see spreadsheet). Rollover sample: up to 25% of unused commit can be applied to next quarter (not cumulative).

Sample cost for Month 2 (if hit commit exactly): 375,000,000 tokens * $0.0000625 = $23,437.50
If surge to 3x but within surge cap: additional 750,000,000 tokens billed at committed rate (no uplift) up to cap.

Notes:
- Cliff protection: for months 1–2, we apply 50% credit on unused commit when switching to the failure-safeguard path (as agreed above).
- Prepay: Finance has the option to take 2% discount for prepaying Month 1 amounts.

Let me know if you want the table broken down by daily expected burn to model short spikes.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Pricing Ops
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Thanks all — this is very helpful and the hybrid schedule looks like a close fit to what we need. A couple of final asks before we route to legal and procurement:

- Can Redwood add a clause that allows rollover credits up to 25% as you suggested, but only for one quarter? Please add explicit language in the SOW.
- Confirm that the surge cap definition (3x) is month-over-month and that the 48-hour sustained fallback to a cost-optimized model is an automated action (we'd like the failover behavior documented).
- Procurement attached our PO intake doc — can you confirm timelines for signature and whether Redwood can accept a net-30?

If those items are accepted, we'll kick the legal review and loop in Ashley (CFO) for final sign-off. Thanks for the quick turn.

Best,
